obligations.statement: For any number of threads, pages and blocks and any interleaving, the page protocol never reaches an integrity stop, never refuses a held block's release, and keeps its invariant.
premises: the C++ memory model's coherence
each segment between step marks atomic
sequentially consistent operations linearizable
the queue and abandoned-list contracts
a caller releases only a block it holds, once (H, per word, is the ghost set of its blocks allocated and not released)
only the page's owner writes its free words, summary and live; another thread writes only a remote word, by fetch_or (each write is one covers finds)
low(x) is x's lowest set bit (the block take_from returns, at countr_zero), and take_from runs on a non-zero word
a sum over the page's words is at least each of its terms, and a counter is not negative
the steps listed are every change of the invariant's words and counters (each write the covers patterns find is cited by a step's lemma)
each segment between step marks is atomic (the step model)

obligations.statement: A page made with its blocks free starts with its count: its full words and its last word's low bits are its capacity, and live is zero.
premises: the plan's words are the capacity in 64-bit words, rounded up, so every word but the last is full (remaining >= 64) and the last holds 1 to 64 blocks
a word with remaining >= 64 is u64_max, the last 2^remaining - 1 (or u64_max when remaining is 64)
obligations.method: sxv's: a finite sum split at its last term; pop of all 64 bits is 64; pop(2^r - 1) = r (the counter and popcount algebra is the allocator study's sxv (stxlib_notes, planning/stx_minmallocpp/SXV_EVALUATION.md, 2026-11-18), re-implemented here; sxv stays study-only (owner, IC decision 6))
obligations.shows: sum + live == capacity
